statements.attributed: Halide perovskites have superior charge transport properties, tunable band structure, and high defect tolerance
statements.quote: Halide perovskites are known for their superior charge transport properties, tunable band structure, and high defect tolerance, which endow them with excellent electrocatalytic activity. Halide perovskites can also regulate structural characteristics by altering the material composition.

statements.attributed: Sn-based halide double perovskites are environmentally friendly and have a narrower band gap than other metal-based halide perovskites
statements.quote: Sn-based halide double perovskites are environmentally friendly and have a narrower band gap than other metal-based halide perovskites, which render better conductivity to them. Moreover, by regulating the p-band center, higher ion/electron conductivity can be achieved, which helps to improve the adsorption and catalytic performance toward LiPSs.

statements.attributed: Employed bulk-phase models for DOS analysis
statements.quote: To demonstrate the intrinsic semiconducting properties through band structure and bandgap calculations, bulk-phase models were employed for DOS analysis. Conversely, surface structural models were adopted for PDOS calculations to assess the p-band center of surface halogens, given that polysulfide adsorption and catalytic mechanisms in LSBs primarily operate at material surfaces. The band gap and DOS for bulk Cs2SnI6 are presented in Fig. 1a.

statements.attributed: Valence electrons of elements exert a direct influence on the efficiency of electron transfer and play a pivotal role in electrocatalytic reactions
statements.quote: Given that the electrocatalytic reaction is essentially an electron transfer process, the valence electrons of elements, serving as electron donors or acceptors, exert a direct influence on the efficiency of electron transfer and play a pivotal role in electrocatalytic reactions. For metal elements, their valence electrons are primarily electrons of d bands, while for nonmetal elements, their valence electrons are the p band electrons.

statements.attributed: The change in valence electrons of halogen elements facilitates the formation and cleavage of bonds during the redox process of LiPSs
statements.quote: Clearly, as the halogen atomic number increases, the p-band centers move even closer to the Fermi level, which can potentially accelerate electron transfer. The change in valence electrons of halogen elements facilitates the formation and cleavage of bonds during the redox process of LiPSs, ultimately enhancing the efficiency of the electrocatalytic process.

statements.attributed: Synthesized Sn-based halide double perovskites by a hydrothermal method
statements.quote: To verify the theoretical calculation results mentioned above, a series of Sn-based halide double perovskites Cs2SnX6 (X = Cl, Br, I) with different halide anions were synthesized by a hydrothermal method. Typical X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns reveal that the diffraction peaks near 2θ = 13°, 26°, and 52° correspond to the (111), (222), and (622) crystal planes of Cs2SnI6 (JCPDS no. 73-0330), respectively (Fig. S1, ESI†).

statements.quote: The Cs2SnI6, Cs2SnBr6, and Cs2SnCl6 modified separators were attached closely to PP with the thicknesses of 16.0, 14.3, and 15.0 μm, respectively (Fig. S10, ESI†). Evidently, Cs2SnX6 (X = Cl, Br, I) and the conductive agent carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were observed to be uniformly distributed across the surface of the separator (Fig. S11, ESI†).

statements.attributed: The migration of LiPSs is effectively inhibited even at high LiPS concentrations, which is undoubtedly ascribed to the robust chemical adsorption capability of Cs2SnI6
statements.quote: In sharp contrast, the electrolyte in the right chamber of the Cs2SnI6 separator always remains almost colorless even after the uninterrupted penetration/diffusion for 12 h, convincingly corroborating that the migration of LiPSs is effectively inhibited even at high LiPS concentrations, which is undoubtedly ascribed to the robust chemical adsorption capability of Cs2SnI6.

statements.attributed: The CV curve displays two distinct cathodic peaks at 2.33 V and 2.03 V, corresponding to the reduction of the S8 ring into soluble LiPSs and further conversion into Li2S2/Li2S
statements.quote: The CV curve displays two distinct cathodic peaks at 2.33 V (peak 1) and 2.03 V (peak 2), corresponding to the reduction of the S8 ring into soluble LiPSs (Li2Sn, 4 ≤ n ≤ 8) and further conversion into Li2S2/Li2S. Besides, the anodic peak appears at 2.34 V (peak 3), which is attributed to the desulfurization of Li2S2/Li2S and Li2Sn.
